To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we define a notion of responsibility that can be used to define a notion of blame, that the degree of responsibility and blame can be computed using a structural-model framework, and that the framework can be used to reason about the degree of responsibility for an action and the degree of blame for a state.

(a) we extend the definition of responsibility introduced by Halper n and Pearl (2005) by introducing a notion of degree, (b) we define a notion of blame as the degree of responsibility, given an agent's episte matic state, (c) we show that blame is transitive and satisfies some other intuitive properties, and (d) we show how to compute blame in some examples.
we have defined and axiomatized notions of degree of responsibility and blame, and have shown that these notions satisfy a number of desirable properties.
